author: Jackson, Frederick H.; Marck, Jeffrey C.
title: Carolinian-English dictionary
notes: In collaboration with Jesus Mareham Elameto, Rosario M. Elameto, Antonio Flores Kaipat, Francisco Mettao Olopai, Margarita O. Sarapau, Teresa I. Taitano and Rosa Roppul Warakai (title page). Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (Open Access edition of 2019, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, in Downloads): the Introduction (pp. xv-xxiv), 'The sounds of Carolinian' (p. 27, read from the page image) and the entries for the letters. Three dialects: Tanapag (TAN, descendants of Namonuito settlers) and two southern ones, the majority EL (Elle, l only) and LN (with both l and n), descended from Satawalese-Lamotrekese and from Puluwatese-Pulusukese settlers; the southern EL dialect is the fullest represented (pp. xv-xxi). Data source of the Carolinian columns of Bender et al. (2003a). The Open Access edition is listed at www.hawaiiopen.org (p. ii).
